network.overall_strategy: The supplied literature strongly supports an all-surface cyanosulfidic route, so this network stays in evaporitic/geothermal surface pools rather than adding unsupported hydrothermal or biochemical detours. To preserve the requested 8-15 molecule scope while retaining the chemistry unique to arginine, the graph begins at 3-aminopropanenitrile, the immediate precursor made upstream in the broader Patel et al. cyanosulfidic system. Cyanamide installs the guanidino functionality, three literature-inspired Cu/H2S cyclization condition variants converge on the same cyclic hemiaminal hub, HCN ring opening and sulfide/thioamide editing remodel the chain, and ammonolysis plus aqueous nitrile hydrolysis deliver racemic arginine.

reactions.name: Cyanamide guanidination of 3-aminopropanenitrile

conditions.other: Concentrating cyanosulfidic pool; cyanamide must reach useful local concentration.

reactions.mechanism: The primary amine attacks cyanamide, followed by proton transfers to furnish the guanidine/amidine motif.
reactions.reasoning: This is the arginine-defining guanidination step in the cyanosulfidic sequence of Patel et al. (2015). It is experimentally grounded and chemically direct, though the literature notes that cyanamide availability and steady-state concentration are important uncertainties.

reactions.name: Cu-assisted cyclization to the cyclic guanidine hemiaminal (variant A)

conditions.other: Concentrated wet-dry surface film on Cu-bearing grains; H2S is treated as the stoichiometric reductant and sulfur is written as S0 for balance.

reactions.mechanism: A guanidine nitrogen attacks the nitrile intramolecularly to close a six-membered ring; hydrolysis and reduction generate the C4 hemiaminal.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) reported Cu/H2S-promoted cyclization of 2-(2-cyanoethyl)guanidine to this cyclic intermediate under one condition set. The explicit H2S to S0 bookkeeping is not given in the paper and is therefore a balanced formalization added here to close mass balance; the core cyclization itself is literature-supported. Copper accessibility on early Earth surfaces remains a known challenge discussed in the review.

reactions.name: Cu-assisted cyclization to the cyclic guanidine hemiaminal (variant B)

conditions.other: More dilute hydrolytic cyanosulfidic pool over native copper or Cu-rich detritus; same balanced net chemistry under a second literature-inspired condition set.

reactions.mechanism: The same ring-closing addition-hydrolysis sequence proceeds in a more aqueous regime to give the cyclic hemiaminal.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) described multiple Cu/H2S-assisted condition variants for formation of the cyclic intermediate. This node represents a second condition family; the balanced small-molecule stoichiometry is again a formal closure of the experimentally observed transformation, with sulfur written as S0 because the original report does not enumerate a complete net redox equation.

reactions.name: Cu-assisted cyclization to the cyclic guanidine hemiaminal (variant C)

conditions.other: Geothermal wet-dry reheating regime; third literature-inspired Cu/H2S cyclization condition set with the same balanced net stoichiometry.

reactions.mechanism: Ring closure, hydrolysis, and reduction again generate the six-membered cyclic hemiaminal intermediate.
reactions.reasoning: This reaction encodes a third Cu/H2S-assisted cyclization variant consistent with Patel et al. (2015). As above, the transformation is experimental, while the explicit sulfur coproduct is a stoichiometric formalization introduced here because the publication reports the conversion but not a fully balanced elemental bookkeeping.

reactions.name: HCN ring opening of the cyclic hemiaminal

conditions.other: HCN-rich surface pool; transient concentration and partial UV shielding favor productive cyanation.

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide attacks the hemiaminal carbon, opening the ring and generating a linear cyanohydrin while retaining the guanidine unit.
reactions.reasoning: This ring-opening/cyanation step is directly aligned with Patel et al. (2015). The product identity is literature-supported, though the review notes that the factors controlling the required regioselective opening are still not fully characterized.

reactions.name: Hydrogen sulfide thiolysis of the nitrile

conditions.other: Sulfide-rich cyanosulfidic pool or hot-spring runoff.

reactions.mechanism: Sulfide adds to the nitrile carbon and, after proton transfer, converts the nitrile into the corresponding thioamide.
reactions.reasoning: Nitrile-to-thioamide conversion by H2S is a hallmark cyanosulfidic transformation and is experimentally supported in the arginine sequence of Patel et al. (2015). This step is one of the better-grounded sulfur-editing reactions in the network.

reactions.name: Cu-assisted reductive dehydroxylation of the hydroxy thioamide

conditions.other: Cu-bearing sulfide-rich surface under wet-dry cycling; sulfur is written as S0 for balanced redox bookkeeping.

reactions.mechanism: Cu-mediated reductive deoxygenation removes the beta-hydroxyl group and gives the saturated thioamide.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) experimentally support Cu/H2S-driven dehydroxylation at this stage. The explicit elemental sulfur product is a balanced formalization of the reductive sulfide chemistry rather than a coproduct explicitly enumerated in the paper, but the underlying transformation is literature-backed.

reactions.name: Cu-assisted thioamide-to-cyanohydrin editing

conditions.other: HCN reintroduced on a sulfide-conditioned copper surface; sulfur extrusion is written as S0 for balance.

reactions.mechanism: The thioamide undergoes hydrolytic editing and cyanation to regenerate a terminal cyanohydrin, while sulfur and ammonia are expelled.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) report the functional conversion of this thioamide stage back to a nitrile/cyanohydrin intermediate under Cu/sulfide/HCN chemistry. Because the paper does not fully specify the net elemental bookkeeping, the explicit S0 byproduct used here is partly speculative and serves as a mass-balanced formalization of the experimentally supported transformation.

reactions.name: Ammonolytic amination to the arginine aminonitrile

conditions.other: Ammonia-rich evaporative pool; substitution at the cyanohydrin center.

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia substitutes for the hydroxyl group at the cyanohydrin center to give the alpha-aminonitrile, with water formed as the leaving-group product.
reactions.reasoning: The amination step is experimentally supported in Patel et al. (2015). Water is written explicitly here because the unbalanced shorthand often omits the leaving-group bookkeeping; the balanced net chemistry is still fully consistent with the reported transformation.

reactions.name: Aqueous nitrile hydrolysis to arginine

conditions.other: Prolonged aqueous heating and rehydration; two water equivalents are inferred stoichiometrically even though water is listed once.

reactions.mechanism: The aminonitrile hydrates stepwise through the usual amide manifold and terminates at the carboxylic acid, releasing ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support final nitrile hydrolysis to arginine under cyanosulfidic aqueous conditions. The compact graph omits the likely transient amide, but the net conversion is literature-grounded; as in the review, the product should be racemic because no enantioselective process is built into this chemistry.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Complete route from the chosen entry point to arginine and strongly aligned overall with Patel et al. The main weakness is rxn_002: it is labeled as cyclization variant A but encoded as a hydrated NH3-releasing Cu/H2S process, so it no longer cleanly represents the literature dry variant. rxn_007 and rxn_008 are plausible surface-cyanosulfidic edits but their sulfur bookkeeping is less directly supported than the cited H2S/Cu formulations, and rxn_010 should explicitly use 2 H2O.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_002 to match the published dry variant A, or relabel it as a generic Cu/H2S cyclization.
Clarify why rxn_007 and rxn_008 produce elemental sulfur rather than the more directly cited H2S/Cu bookkeeping.
Write rxn_010 as mol_014 + 2 mol_006 -> mol_015 + mol_004.

Make Cu and the Cu/H2S redox role explicit in rxn_007 and rxn_008.

evaluation.network_feedback: Strong, literature-grounded surface cyanosulfidic subnetwork from 3-aminopropanenitrile to arginine; given the stated scope, starting at this immediate precursor is acceptable. The graph is connected, molecule IDs are consistent, and the RDKit check reports no unbalanceable reactions; rxn_010 is balanceable but should be written as mol_014 + 2 mol_006 -> mol_015 + mol_004. Chemistry and environmental placement align closely with Patel et al. (2015), and no cross-environment transfers are needed. The main deductions are representational rather than fatal: rxn_002-rxn_004 are partly redundant as encoded and do not cleanly preserve the published differences among cyclization variants A, B, and C, rxn_007-rxn_008 render sulfur bookkeeping more abstractly than the cited Cu/H2S formulations, Cu is only implicit, and the network does not explicitly note racemic output or practical challenges such as Cu availability and multistep yield loss. Overall this is a good, chemically plausible network, but these annotation and stoichiometry issues keep it below the >=0.9 approval threshold.
